title: Wednesday 18 November summary
text:
Good morning, it is Wednesday eighteen November: this is the GERICO summary.

Let us start with the Gulf. Between Tuesday and Wednesday, the United States and Iran exchanged strikes. An American official says that US aircraft struck a missile base on the Iranian island of Qeshm, in response to an attack on Bahrain. Iran claims to have also struck an American base in Kuwait. Bahrain and Kuwait speak of intercepted attacks.

Moving on to China. In Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met on the eve of the three-way meeting with Donald Trump, scheduled for Thursday. Putin said Western sanctions have failed. Washington points to Iran and nuclear disarmament as topics, and Trump said Ukraine will also be discussed.

On Ukraine, US Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby said in Brussels that deep Ukrainian strikes inside Russia do not work. German minister Boris Pistorius and British minister Wes Streeting rejected the criticism.

In Italy, the Chamber of Deputies gave final approval to the law on antisemitism, with one hundred and forty-seven votes in favour and ninety-three against. And the majority is presenting an amendment today to ban social media for children under thirteen.

Moving on to the markets. Wall Street closed down yesterday for the second day: the Dow Jones lost 1.6%, the S&P 500 1% and the Nasdaq 0.7%. Weighing on the market were Nvidia and other artificial intelligence stocks.

After the close, however, Nvidia beat expectations, with revenue of 115.8 billion and shares rising by 2.3% in after-hours trading. The board, meanwhile, ruled out the return of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

In Asia, Tokyo opened up 0.25% this morning, while Hong Kong shed more than 2%.

In Europe, stock markets closed sharply down yesterday: Frankfurt minus 2.08%, London minus 1.76%, Paris minus 1.62% and Milan minus 1.31%, with the FTSE MIB at 50,845 points. The spread between BTPs and Bunds stands at 105 bp.

On the foreign exchange market, the yen is stable at 159.50 to the dollar. For gold, oil, euro-dollar and the pound we do not have verified quotes from this morning: on oil, the AP agency writes only that it rose yesterday.

Today at 8:00 British inflation data are released. At 16:00 Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey speaks. At 20:00 the minutes of the latest Fed meeting are expected.

The full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
